title: refactor: move shared state out of the protocol.ts and engine.ts facades into state-owning facets, so the hot bodies left on the class can become delegations (ruling 6624345766)
body:
domain:server#6 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5

Filing gate: ruling 6624345766 on #29465 item (4). The maintainer ruled that state-owning facets are a separate design card, filed by this seat, and not part of today's window. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.
Ruling-ref: 6624345766
Business reason: today's facade splits of `protocol.ts` (#29985) and `engine.ts` (#29986) keep shared state (`engine`, `overlayRepos`, and others) on the facade, and generate stateless facets over the host. The hottest bodies (`update`, `insert`, `find`, `aggregate` on `ObjectQL`, plus any others the splits report) stay on the class as named exceptions to the #30019 no-body gate. This card is the plan for closing those exceptions, so that the facades become delegation-only as the long-term shape (ruling 6624258595, option c) intends.
Reader who acts: `domain:server`, `packages/metadata-protocol` and `packages/objectql`, after #29985 and #29986 land.
Dedupe (open and closed): `state-owning facet`, `facade state`, `29465`. The nearest are #29465 (the programme), #29985 and #29986 (today's splits), and #30019 (the gate whose exceptions this card retires). **New.**

## What to design

- **A state-ownership rule.** Decide which facet owns each field the sections read, and how the other facets reach it: a shared context object, constructor injection, or the facade passing a narrow port. The 190 hand-series stubs that build local `.call(host, …)` objects need the same rule.
- **The proof.** Bodies have to be rewritten here, so byte-identity no longer holds. Use an undo proof instead: undoing the rewrite rebuilds today's body. Keep the public-surface `.d.ts` bar of 6624345766 and the suites and gates at base counts.
- **Order.** One exception per PR, or one facet per PR. Each PR removes its rows from the #30019 allow-list.

Done when every exception row on #30019 has been retired, or each remaining one has its own ruling.
